subject: english-language
title: Writing to Persuade Adventure
welcome_lead: Now apply the toolkit — write articles and speeches that actually convince people.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language transactional writing — AFOREST, structure, persuasive openings.
final_note: You practised structuring persuasive texts and using AFOREST to convince a reader.

concepts.def: Letter (Dear Sir/Madam), article (headline, byline), speech (direct address), report; conventions matter.
Inform, persuade, argue, explain, advise; word choice shifts; persuasive uses emotive language.
Adjust register: formal for parliament, informal for peers; vocabulary, examples, references.
Article opens with attention-grabbing headline (often pun); subheadings break up text.
Opens paragraph stating main idea; rest develops it; clear navigation for reader.
Acknowledge opposing view ('Some may argue...'); then refute; builds credibility in argument.

walkthroughs.body_html: Remember AFOREST: Alliteration, Facts, Opinions, Rhetorical questions, Emotive language, Stats, Triplets.

Hook readers with a shocking statistic or rhetorical question.

End with a punchy call to action: 'Sign the petition. Today.'

Acknowledge the other side: 'Of course, some argue.' then dismantle it: '.but the evidence shows otherwise.'

This makes you sound fair AND right.
